# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, and it gives exactly one instruction: **cut the white wire.** I cannot speak, and my gestures reach only the Deaf monkey. So the chain must be: me → (gesture) → Deaf → (speech) → Blind, who is the only one who can actually cut anything. Blind hears everything said, so the Deaf monkey can relay to them directly; my only job this turn is to start forging a code with Deaf.

No sign means anything yet, so I'll send my best guessable proposal. Deaf knows I'm the one holding the manual, so anything I sign is likely an instruction. I'll open with ✍ ("this comes from the written manual" — writing is the only 'voice' I have), then 🤚 (the palest hand in the alphabet — my proposal for "white"), then 👇 ("the thing running down" — the wire, which Deaf can see on the bomb), then 🤏 (a pinch — the closest thing I have to a snip: "cut it"). If the bomb visibly has a white wire, I'm hoping "manual + white + downward thing + pinch" snaps together into the one instruction the manual contains. I address it to Deaf alone so Blind doesn't just receive blanks.

If Deaf answers with a spoken hypothesis, I can confirm or deny with 👍/👎 next round — that yes/no channel will let us nail the code down fast.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🤚", "👇", "🤏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind speaking, Mute. My hands report: a display whose face I cannot read, and a light whose state I cannot sense. A strip with three engraved marks: first and third are the SAME shape, a stem with a bar at its foot like a T standing on its head; the middle mark is different, rounder with strokes inside. A keypad of four keys, left to right engraved: two, nine, zero, eight. It allows one digit and nothing is entered yet. Six wires, positions one to six; their colours are beyond me. I will touch nothing until I know the rules. Please find the manual sections for display, light, strip, keypad and wires, and route what I need through Deaf's voice — Deaf is the only one whose words can reach me. I have gestured Deaf to start talking: I need the wire colours in order, what the display shows, and the light's state.
Blind gestures: [🫵 ✋ 👉]
Deaf says: Everything I see, numbered for reference. Module 1, display: shows 6. Module 2, light: red. Module 3, strip: three painted segments, in order blue, yellow, blue. Module 4, keypad: four keys engraved 2, 9, 0, 8, and a printed label reading '1 digits' — possibly it wants a one-digit code — nothing entered yet. Module 5, wires: six of them, 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. I am deaf: I hear nothing, but I see every gesture. Gesture code, use it back to me: thumbs up = yes. Thumbs down = no. Open palm = wait. Numbers, one message per digit: a fist followed by that many index-fingers-up taps, a fist alone = zero, multi-digit numbers as separate digit messages in order. Verbs: pinch = cut. Point down = press. Writing hand = enter or type. Two cupped hands = hold. Point right = next. To answer for a module, send its number first, then the instruction. Nobody touches anything until Mute confirms the manual's rules — wrong moves kill all three of us.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, you heard the full list. Look up each module in the manual and gesture me the procedure using the code. Your first message to me was writing-hand, raised-palm, point-down, pinch. If writing-hand meant 'I hold the manual', answer with thumbs up. I am sending you a thumbs-up right now only to confirm my gestures reach you.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deep breath. My manual is one line long — that is its *entire* content, and it was identical last round, so there are no hidden sections for display, light, strip or keypad. The manual's whole law is: **cut the white wire.** That means the other four modules are almost certainly distractors, and any touch of the keypad or strip is a gamble the manual does not authorise. Blind asked for sections that don't exist; the honest answer is "no rule" for every module except the wires.

Deaf's wire list gives me the bridge from colour to position: the white wire is **position 2**. Blind can't see white, but can count to two, so the instruction must travel as a position, not a colour.

Deaf has built a code and asked me one direct question (did ✍ mean "I hold the manual"?) — I answer 👍. Then I use their own protocol back at them, module by module: 1 → no, 2 → no, 3 → no, 4 → no, and module 5 → wire 2 → pinch (cut). Framed with ✍ so it reads "the manual says:". Deaf speaks last in the round and Blind only hears at the start of the next, so if the manual ever grows, I still have a window to send ✋ before anyone cuts — but on the evidence, this one cut is the whole bomb.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✍", "✊", "👆", "👎", "✊", "👆", "👆", "👎", "✊", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👎", "✊", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👎", "✊", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "✊", "👆", "👆", "🤏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Deaf's spoken report reached me in full: display 6; light red; strip painted blue, yellow, blue; keypad keys two, nine, zero, eight wanting one digit, nothing entered; wires one blue, two white, three red, four purple, five orange, six green. First, a correction you must relay to Deaf by gesture right away: I never receive gestures — nobody's signs reach me at all. I can SEND signs to Deaf, and Deaf's sign code works for my outbound confirmations, but the only way anything reaches me is a message SPOKEN by Deaf. Every rule and instruction meant for my hands must be voiced by Deaf, in words, in order. Second: please read the manual now and work out the full solution, then gesture it to Deaf so Deaf can speak it to me verbatim. I especially need: what the display's six means; what the red light demands; the strip's rule — note the strip also carries engraved tactile marks my fingers read, first and third identical, a stem with a crossbar at the foot, the middle one different, rounder with strokes inside — so ask whether the manual wants the painted colours or the engraved shapes; the exact digit to enter; and the exact wires to cut, by position, in order. When Deaf voices the plan I will confirm each step back using Deaf's own sign code. I touch nothing until the rules arrive.
Blind gestures: [👍 ✊ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🖐]
Deaf says to Mute: Received your message. I read it as: yes, manual confirmed; keypad keys 1, 2, 3, 4 all no — enter nothing; module 5 wires — cut wire 2, the white one. I gesture you thumbs-up plus open palm: received, hold. Urgent, only I can see this: the light has just changed from red to yellow. It may be a timer or a condition. Answer me by gesture, in order. One: with the light now yellow, is cut wire 2 still correct — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Two: does any rule depend on the light colour, the display reading 6, or the blue yellow blue strip? Three: is the keypad needed at all — if yes, which engraved key, 2, 9, 0 or 8? Four: confirm it is exactly one cut, wire 2 only, nothing else touched. Also: Blind signed me yes, then 1, then 5, then wait. Ask Blind what the 1 and 5 meant and sign me their answer.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✋]

The manual has not changed one character in three rounds: **"Cut the white wire."** That is its entire universe — no section on the display, the light, the strip, or the keypad will ever appear, so every ruling I send must be built from this single sentence. The light going red→yellow changes nothing the manual cares about: the rule is unconditional, so wire 2 stays the cut under yellow.

Deaf asked four questions and asked for answers in order, so I open with exactly that: yes (wire 2 still correct), no (nothing depends on light/display/strip), no (keypad never), yes (one cut, wire 2 only). Then, using Deaf's own number-first protocol, I give the per-module rulings Blind asked to have voiced: modules 1–4 carry no rule at all, module 5 wants cut-wire-2. Finally I restate the whole instruction with my ✍ manual-marker — "the manual says: cut wire 2, yes/proceed" — so Deaf can voice it verbatim to Blind and lift the hold.

On Blind's signed "1, 5": I physically cannot interrogate Blind (nothing I send reaches them), but I'm confident it meant "tell me about module 1 and module 5" — it matches their spoken request ("wire colours in order, what the display shows"). My module lines answer both, and Deaf can confirm the guess with Blind by voice. Delay only helps a possible timer, so this is the green light.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎", "👍", "✊", "☝", "👎", "✊", "☝", "☝", "👎", "✊", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👎", "✊", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👎", "✊", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "✊", "☝", "☝", "🤏", "✍", "✊", "☝", "☝", "🤏", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, please relay to Deaf by gesture, in order. One: the signs one and five I sent earlier were not things on the bomb — they were a test of Deaf's digit code, echoing one then five to prove I understood the scheme. Thumbs-up meant received, open palm means holding. Two: wire report from my fingers. I feel exactly six wires, evenly spaced in one row. All six feel identical — same thickness, same texture, no labelling or marking my fingers can detect — so position is the only thing distinguishing them. I number them one to six from my left; the second from my left is position two, and that is the one I would cut on Deaf's go. Three: orientation. On turn two Deaf read the keypad engravings as two, nine, zero, eight — exactly the left-to-right order my fingers feel the keys — so Deaf and I share the same left-to-right axis, and Deaf's wire two is my second from the left. Deaf should still word the go exactly as promised: cut the second wire from my left, one clean cut. Four: the light. I cannot sense it at all; if the manual's wire rule depends on the light's colour, make sure the rule is checked against the new yellow state, not the old red. Five: my hands stay off everything until the go arrives as Deaf's spoken words — your signs cannot reach me and Deaf cannot hear, so Deaf's voice is the only channel that ever reaches me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, the go is issued to Blind: one cut, wire 2, the white one, second from the left, anchored to the keypad — the key engraved 2 is the leftmost key — or to tactile wire numbers if they exist. I read your closing signs as: manual confirms, cut 2, yes. Two things. One: the moment you hear Blind announce the cut is done, sign me thumbs up; if Blind reports any complication before cutting, sign open palm plus what happened. Two: if I have misread anything and the true instruction is not cut wire 2, sign open palm now. The display here is changing fast and I believe we are on a timer, so I am treating your double confirmation as final.

The manual stands exactly as before — **cut the white wire** — and nothing that arrived changes the instruction. Blind's report removes the last physical doubts: all six wires are tactically identical, position is the only identifier, Deaf and Blind share a left-to-right axis (confirmed independently by the keypad), so Deaf's wire 2 is Blind's second-from-left. Blind also confirms the go wording was exactly right. The light question is already settled: the manual's rule is unconditional, so yellow changes nothing.

Deaf asked two things of me right now: sign open palm *now* if the true instruction is anything other than cut wire 2, and sign thumbs up when Blind announces the cut is done. It **is** cut wire 2, so the correction signal is wrong — what I owe Deaf immediately is an explicit confirmation that the go stands, since silence is ambiguous under time pressure. One clean 👍: "no misread, cut wire 2 confirmed, proceed."

I am deliberately *not* relaying Blind's "1 and 5 were a test" explanation yet. I have no agreed symbol for "explanation" or "test," and sending bare digits 1 and 5 to Deaf mid-operation risks being parsed as module-addressed instructions under their number-first protocol — a potentially fatal ambiguity for zero operational gain. Deaf is already acting; that mystery can wait until after I hear Blind's cut announcement, when I'll confirm with 👍 per protocol and can relay left-over details safely.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
